entry.title: Adversarial Robustness in Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey
entry.summary: We present a comprehensive survey of adversarial robustness techniques for large language models (LLMs). Our analysis covers prompt injection attacks, jailbreaking methods, and defense mechanisms including input sanitization and output filtering. We evaluate 15 state-of-the-art models across multiple attack vectors and propose a unified taxonomy for classifying adversarial threats in the LLM ecosystem.

entry.title: Zero-Knowledge Proofs for Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning Inference
entry.summary: This paper introduces a novel framework for applying zero-knowledge proofs to verify machine learning model inference without revealing the model weights or input data. We demonstrate practical performance on convolutional neural networks with accuracy loss below 0.1% while providing cryptographic guarantees of correctness.

entry.title: Detecting Supply Chain Attacks in Open Source Dependencies Using Graph Neural Networks
entry.summary: We propose a graph neural network-based approach for detecting malicious packages in open source software supply chains. Our method constructs dependency graphs enriched with behavioral features extracted from package metadata and code analysis. Evaluated on a dataset of 50,000 npm packages, our approach achieves 97.3% precision and 94.1% recall in identifying compromised dependencies.
